newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian govt not paralysed by scandal - minister.
newsitem.headline: Belgian govt not paralysed by scandal - minister.

text.p: Belgian Social Affairs Minister Magda de Galan said on Tuesday that a fresh scandal hitting the francophone PS socialist party was not paralysing the government.
"We still carry on with our work. The cabinet of ministers has not been paralysed," said de Galan, a member of the PS.
"I'm not saying there is nothing, but work goes on. I think it's important because 1997 is an important year, not just for Maastricht," she told BRTN radio.

Heads of state and governments will decide in early 1998, on the basis of whether fiscal and monetary performance in 1997 sufficiently meets the Maastricht Treaty criteria, which countries will initially qualify for a single European currency.
The PS is the second most powerful partner in Belgium's four-party centre-left coalition government with the Flemish Socialists and the Walloon and Flemish Christian Democratic parties.

Opposition leaders have urged the government, led by Flemish Christian Democrat (CVP) Jean-Luc Dehaene, to quit following the arrest of two leading PS officials as part of a probe into allegations the PS received kickbacks from French aviation firm Dassault.

Belgian newspapers said on Tuesday that the scandal, which they said also indirectly implicated Walloon regional government president Guy Spitaels, a former PS president, was putting more and more pressure on the government.

De Galan said the PS had "received the message loud and clear" from Dehaene and CVP president Marc Van Peel, that the PS should clean up its act and make clear within the next few days who was to blame for the scandal.
"We know what we have to do," she said, without elaborating.
She also dismissed calls by a liberal opposition leader for the government to resign as "a bit of frustration at being so long in the opposition".
